provider: openICPSR (ICPSR, University of Michigan) — self-publishing repository

free_tier.stated: 30 GB per file with a 30 GB total per deposit and 1,000 files/folders per deposit; explicitly 'no cost to you'. Because deposits are unlimited and instant, the effective ceiling is per-deposit, not per-person.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: no retention statement was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that retention is unlimited
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free, 'no cost dissemination to other data users'. Downloads are immediate and public in the format submitted; no egress pricing exists in the product. Restricted-use options exist but are optional.

tooling: Web upload plus 'Import From Zip' bulk extractor (1,000 files/folders per zip), versioning with a new DOI per version, and the underlying ICPSR deposit pipeline. No public rclone backend; automation is a scripted HTTP/form loop rather than a documented S3-style API — this is the weak point versus RepOD.
chaining: Unlimited deposits x 30 GB each. 17 deposits = 510 GB; no account-level aggregate is published, and requests above 30 GB go to ICPSR Acquisitions for approval rather than being refused outright.
limits_note: Per-object-cap 30 GB/file; per-deposit 30 GB and 1,000 files; ZIP extraction capped at 1,000 entries. Content is scope-gated to social/behavioural/health sciences and replication data, and every deposit gets a DOI, so deposits are citable publications rather than scratch storage.

Priority seam: a university or national repository whose deposit door is open to anyone and whose write path is an API.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
